He was a college standout for the [[Marquette Golden Eagles men's basketball|Marquette Golden Eagles]]. ==High school career== Hayward went to [[Buffalo Traditional High School]] where he was an outstanding basketball player. After graduating from Buffalo Traditional in 2004, Hayward enrolled in [[Notre Dame Preparatory School (Fitchburg, Massachusetts)|Notre Dame Prep School]] in [[Fitchburg, Massachusetts]], as only the [[NCAA Division III]] college [[SUNY Fredonia]] expressed any interest in Hayward. Hayward attended [[Notre Dame Preparatory School (Fitchburg, Massachusetts)|Notre Dame Prep School]] in [[Fitchburg, Massachusetts]], and while he attended he played with many other notable players, like [[Michael Beasley]], [[Syracuse University]] standout [[Paul Harris (basketball)|Paul Harris]] and [[UTEP]] player [[Derrick Caracter]]. Hayward started both freshman and sophomore seasons. Considered a four-star recruit by [[Rivals.com]], Hayward was listed as the No. 18 small forward and the No. 73 player in the nation in 2006.{{cite web|title=Lazar Hayward Recruiting Profile|url=https://sports.yahoo.com/footballrecruiting/basketball/recruiting/player-Lazar-Hayward-39578|access-date=January 29, 2016|work=Yahoo.com}} ==College career== At [[Marquette University]], Hayward received the nickname "Money Man". He finished his Marquette career as the program's 3rd all-time leading scorer and 5th all time in rebounds, as well as garnering 2nd-Team All-[[Big East Conference|Big East]] honors in 2008 and 2010 and Honorable Mention AP All-American status in 2010 while leading Marquette to 4 NCAA Tournament appearances. On April 2, 2010, Hayward was named the Hershey's Player of the Game in the [[Reese's College All-Star Game]].{{cite web|title=2010 Reese's College All-Star Game|url=http://grfx.cstv.com/photos/schools/nabc/genrel/auto_pdf/2010asg.pdf|work=cbssports.com/mcc|publisher=CBS Sports|access-date=11 April 2013|archive-date=October 4, 2013|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20131004213058/http://grfx.cstv.com/photos/schools/nabc/genrel/auto_pdf/2010asg.pdf|url-status=dead}} ==Professional career== === Minnesota Timberwolves (2010–2011) === On June 25, 2010, Hayward was selected by the [[Washington Wizards]] with the 30th pick in the [[2010 NBA draft]], but his draft rights were traded to the [[Minnesota Timberwolves]] shortly after being drafted.{{cite news|title=Minnesota Acquires Draft Rights to Lazar Hayward|url=http://www.nba.com/timberwolves/news/Minnesota_Acquires_Draft_Rights_to_Lazar_Hayward_2010_06_25.html|access-date=January 29, 2016|work=NBA.com|date=June 25, 2010}} In 2011, his college teammate [[Jimmy Butler]] was taken with the same pick in the NBA draft. It was the first time Marquette players went back-to-back in the first round since [[Bo Ellis]] was drafted by Washington in 1977 and [[Butch Lee]] was taken by Atlanta in 1978. In his first season in the NBA, he averaged 3.8 points in 10 minutes per game for the Timberwolves. === Oklahoma City Thunder (2011–2012) === On December 13, 2011, before the start of another season, Hayward was traded to the Oklahoma City Thunder for two second-round draft picks and [[Robert Vaden (basketball)|Robert Vaden]].{{cite news|title=Timberwolves Trade Lazar Hayward to Oklahoma City|url=http://www.nba.com/timberwolves/news/hayward_trade_okc_2011_12_13.html|access-date=January 29, 2016|work=NBA.com|date=June 25, 2010}} The Thunder assigned Hayward to the [[Tulsa 66ers]] of the D-League on March 2, 2012.{{cite news|title=Oklahoma City Thunder assign forward Lazar Hayward to the Tulsa 66ers |url=http://www.kjrh.com/dpp/sports/local_sports/oklahoma-city-thunder-assign-forward-lazar-hayward-to-the-tulsa-66ers |access-date=March 2, 2012 |work=KJRH.com |date=March 2, 2012 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120306145225/http://www.kjrh.com/dpp/sports/local_sports/oklahoma-city-thunder-assign-forward-lazar-hayward-to-the-tulsa-66ers |archive-date=March 6, 2012 }} The Thunder recalled him on March 4, 2012, after he averaged 28 ppg in 2 games with the Tulsa 66ers.{{cite news|title=Thunder Recall Lazar Hayward|url=http://basketball.realgm.com/wiretap/219416/Thunder-Recall-Lazar-Hayward|access-date=January 29, 2016|work=RealGM.com|date=March 4, 2012}} With the Thunder that season, he averaged 1.4 points per game, shooting 34% from the field. Hayward reached the [[2012 NBA Finals]] with the Thunder, but the team lost to the [[Miami Heat]]. === Return to Minnesota (2012–2013) === On October 27, 2012, Hayward was traded to the [[Houston Rockets]]{{cite news|title=Thunder trade Harden to Rockets for Martin, Lamb and 6, 2013}} but re-signed two days later on a 10-day contract.{{cite news|title=Wolves Sign Lazar Hayward To 10-Day Contract|url=http://www.nba.com/timberwolves/news/wolves-sign-lazar-hayward-10-day-contract|access-date=January 8, 2013|work=NBA.com|date=January 8, 2013}} === Los Angeles D-Fenders (2013; 2016) === After the 10-day contract expired, Hayward joined the [[Los Angeles D-Fenders]] of the [[NBA Development League]].{{cite news|title=Lazar Hayward returns to Los Angeles Pelicans]].{{cite web|title=PELICANS ANNOUNCE 2013 TRAINING CAMP ROSTER|url=http://www.nba.com/pelicans/news/pelicans-announce-2013-training-camp-roster|access-date=September 30, 2013|work=NBA.com|date=September 30, 2013}} He was later waived by the Pelicans on October 13, 2013.{{cite news|title=PELICANS WAIVE LAZAR the Nets. In 20 games, he averaged 12.5 points, 5.9 rebounds and 1.4 steals in 24.3 minutes.{{cite web|url=http://longisland.dleague.nba.com/news/long-island-nets-acquire-prince-ibeh-waive-lazar-hayward/|title=Long Island Nets Acquire Prince Ibeh, Waive Lazar Hayward|work=NBA.com|date=February 8,
